$comment: infra/environments.json (owned by bl-devops). Names and rules only, never values. Values are set by Matthew in Vercel, GitHub and the orchestrator's .env.local (docs/ops/account-setup.md). scripts/env-check.mjs reads this file. scope: app = Vercel runtime variable; system = provided by Vercel, never set by hand; ci = GitHub environment secret/variable (must be absent from Vercel); orchestrator = .env.local on the orchestrator machine and/or GitHub (must be absent from Vercel). production/preview rules: required | optional | absent. githubEnvs: the GitHub environments (or 'repo') that hold the name.

production.deploys: only by .github/workflows/release.yml after Gate 3 and Matthew's approval; Git deploys of main are off in vercel.json

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
variables.note: production: production project URL; preview: staging project URL

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
variables.note: publishable key of the matching project

variables.name: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
variables.note: read only in src/lib/server/admin.ts (SECURITY_MODEL invariant 2)

variables.name: SITE_URL
variables.note: two rows: production address, staging address

variables.name: APP_SIGNING_SECRET
variables.note: SEC-4, at least 32 characters, a different value per environment, Vercel only (never GitHub, never an agent machine)

variables.name: CRON_SECRET
variables.note: SEC-4, at least 32 characters, a different value per environment, Vercel only

variables.name: GHL_PRIVATE_INTEGRATION_TOKEN
variables.note: test sub-account token, scopes contacts.readonly and contacts.write only; a later setting request. Becomes required before the first release that must copy to GHL (DEP1 decides)

variables.name: GHL_LOCATION_ID
variables.note: test sub-account id, not secret, same value in both

variables.name: GHL_API_BASE_URL
variables.note: optional; never set in production (ignored there, SECURITY_MODEL invariant 9)

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_MOCKING
variables.note: frontend lane only: `on` runs the screens against mock handlers (src/mocks/flag.ts). Never set in Production, never on the staging branch (QA and Matthew test the real API there). Unset means off. OPS1 (Nov 27): declared after the frontend lane landed it; env-check had failed `verify` with 'undeclared'

variables.name: VERCEL_ENV
variables.note: Vercel system variable (Automatically expose System Environment Variables)

variables.name: VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA
variables.note: Vercel system variable; /api/health version

variables.name: VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET
variables.note: Protection Bypass for Automation, from the Vercel project; sent as x-vercel-protection-bypass to staging only

variables.name: SUPABASE_STAGING_URL
variables.note: staging project URL, for tests

variables.name: SUPABASE_STAGING_ANON_KEY
variables.note: staging publishable key, for tests

variables.name: SUPABASE_STAGING_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
variables.note: staging secret key, for tests

variables.name: SUPABASE_STAGING_DB_URL
variables.note: staging session-pooler URI with password; migrations and RLS tests (npm run db:migrate, db:test); also in the orchestrator's .env.local

variables.name: SUPABASE_STAGING_REF
variables.note: staging project ref (not secret); db.mjs refuses a staging URL that does not name it

variables.name: SUPABASE_PROD_PROJECT_REF
variables.note: optional guard on the orchestrator machine only: db.mjs refuses a staging URL that names the production project

variables.name: PRODUCTION_HOSTS
variables.note: production hostnames, so QA tooling refuses to run against them

variables.name: STAGING_URL
variables.note: QA's base URL. In CI qa-smoke.yml sets it from the deployment; on the orchestrator machine it is in .env.local

variables.name: QA_OWNER_EMAIL
variables.note: staging owner test login (QA names, proposed by DevOps; QA confirms)

variables.name: QA_OWNER_PASSWORD
variables.note: staging owner test password. REQUIRED in CI since OPS1 (Nov 27): api-tests runs tests/api/auth/sign-in.test.ts and staff-me.test.ts, which sign in for real

variables.name: QA_HELPER_EMAIL
variables.note: staging helper test login

variables.name: QA_HELPER_PASSWORD
variables.note: staging helper test password. REQUIRED in CI since OPS1 (see QA_OWNER_PASSWORD)

variables.name: SUPABASE_PRODUCTION_DB_URL
variables.note: token A: production session-pooler URI with password; lives ONLY in the GitHub production environment; migrations in release.yml

variables.name: VERCEL_TOKEN
variables.note: release token, team baseleap only, 30-day expiry; also read-only drift check in release.yml

variables.name: VERCEL_ORG_ID
variables.note: Vercel team id (not secret)

variables.name: VERCEL_PROJECT_ID
variables.note: Vercel project id (not secret)

variables.name: PRODUCTION_URL
variables.note: repo-level variable, read by release.yml (its pre-flight fails when it is empty) and uptime.yml

variables.name: RELEASE_PREFLIGHT_TOKEN
variables.note: OPTIONAL fallback, create only if release.yml's pre-flight reports that GitHub refused the workflow token (403/404): a fine-grained token for this repository only, permission Actions: Read, nothing else. Repository-level secret (a production-environment secret would only be readable after the approval gate)

vercelConfig.$comment: What vercel.json must say (docs/architecture.md 'Lane ownership'). Headers are next.config.ts's, not vercel.json's.
